subject: SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph
notes: Rule (cite.py --check 12.3.7.4 "If more than one character has the lowest position in the program collating sequence, the first character specified is associated with the figurative constant LOW-VALUE" -> OK §12.3.7.4 9)): lowest ordinal position in the PCS -> LOW-VALUE; tie -> first character specified. CODE: Extremes takes specOrder[0] - the first character specified always occupies position 0 (AlphabetLiteralPhrase assigns positions in source order; a refused duplicate (SR14 a) never enters specOrder; a THRU+ALSO entry refused by COBOL2242 contributes nothing), and a position-0 ALSO tie resolves to that same character. Identity sequences (NATIVE / STANDARD-1/2 / UCS-4 / ASCII) -> U+0000, the lowest native code unit. MEASURED (probe/snp3/g9also.cob): ALPHABET AL IS "B" ALSO "A" ALSO "Z", ... -> LOW-VALUE = 'B' (tie, first specified); (probe/snp3/g9loc.cob) ALPHABET LOC IS LOCALE as PCS -> ORD(LOW-VALUE) = 1 and X"01" = LOW-VALUE (U+0000 shares the lowest, completely-ignorable rank with other C0 controls; U+0000 is the lowest code among them - the locale sequence has no 'specified' order, CONFORMANCE.md §3 L7 documents LOW-VALUE U+0000 under a locale sequence). da1_alphabet_hex_thru derives LOW-VALUE = 'Z' for ALPHABET AL IS X"5A" THRU X"41" from the lowest position (spec-derived expected).
